string.text: Intelligence is the chance that a stalker makes the right decision in a fight. It grows with his Rank, and even a legend sometimes gets it wrong. Personality is how his faction fights, after the character types GSC designed for the Zone. Some factions hold their ground, others press or run, and two stalkers of the same faction can still fight differently.
This sets the chance that a novice makes the right decision, and each higher rank adds to it. The chance stops at 75 percent, whatever the Rank.
Each rank above novice adds this much to the chance of the right decision.

Push and Pull act on weak moments in a fight, against you or another stalker. Push presses an enemy who cannot answer, and Pull draws a stalker back while he is the weak one. Each ends when the moment passes.
Attackers fire longer bursts at a target who cannot answer, and move to closer cover when he bleeds or turns his back. (Intelligence, Personality)
Push on reload and empty mag
The push starts when his target reloads or runs empty, and ends when the weapon is back up.
Healthy attackers close in on a badly hurt target to finish the fight, until he recovers.
A stalker who is reloading, or hurt after a hit, falls back to farther cover while his enemy is strong, and the pull ends when he recovers. (Intelligence, Personality)

Commitment keeps a stalker on a fire action while it still works, where vanilla re-plans every moment and swaps cover over small differences. He switches as soon as he loses sight, his shot is blocked or his enemy is gone. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

Conduct gives disciplined stalkers better habits at moments vanilla already decides, in how they hold cover and how close they fight. A stalker has the discipline for life or not at all, and trained military factions have it most often. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

An experienced rifleman or sniper crouches to fire when the crouched line to his enemy is clear, and stands to fire over low cover that blocks it. Vanilla picks the posture without checking that line. (Intelligence, Personality)
A disciplined stalker picks cover that suits his weapon, closer with a submachine gun, and farther with a sniper rifle as his rank rises. (Intelligence, Personality)

Reaction gives each rank a different aim, in how fast the barrel follows a moving target, how tightly it holds a strafing one, and how well he leads a runner. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

Discipline gives each rank a different trigger, and higher ranks fire shorter bursts more often while low ranks stay at vanilla. The settings keep every rank's rate of fire at or above vanilla. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
Planned: stalkers answer and open fire as far as their weapon reaches. Today a stalker shot from beyond the fight range can only take cover. There is no setting yet.
Planned: player-facing combat feedback, concussion first. Nothing to configure yet.

How often mutants act on an opening, and how much their moves vary. Each species page lists its moves in three groups: NEW MOVES are attacks the vanilla game never fires for that species, MANAGED MOVES are the creature's own attacks this mod decides when to fire, INFLUENCED MOVES are the creature's own abilities whose numbers Wild spreads between individuals. Every move's tooltip names its gates: int (Intelligence decides when), pers (the creature's own leaning toward it), and wild (the values vary).

A mutant's toughness, scaled by the map rank (rookie maps rank 0 up to endgame maps rank 5): damage resistance grows by the slider's percent per rank. Multiplies the installed balance, so other mutant overhauls keep their numbers.
Attacks the vanilla game never fires for this creature. Intelligence and Personality decide, Wild spreads the force.
This creature already has these attacks. AlifeTactics decides when, by Intelligence and Personality.
This creature already has these abilities. Wild spreads their numbers between individuals.

The chance a mutant answers an opening with the right move, before the rank bonus. Observing is free, deciding is hard. Every mutant sees your reload, but only a passed roll turns it into the right answer, and a missed roll lets the opening go, or panics into a flee. One decision every few seconds.
Added to the Intelligence chance for each map rank.

How much a mutant's own numbers vary between individuals: the timings of its moves, how hard it leaps and steers in the air, and the ranges, bands, and reach of its abilities. At 0 every value sits at its band middle, so a kind is identical and learnable. At 100 each spawn and each use rolls any point across its band, so no two read alike.
Hit power grows by this percent for each map rank: rank 0 stays vanilla, rank 5 gets 5 times this bonus.
Damage a mutant receives shrinks by this percent for each map rank, so a deep-Zone mutant shrugs off fire a Cordon one would feel.

The jump up at an enemy on a rock or ledge, with a wind-up. The crouch is the warning a perched player sees, and the leap flies at the game's own force so it clears the edge. Every leaping species can take each leap; its Personality, rolled once per individual, decides which ones it carries. (int, pers)
An instant pounce with no wind-up, at where the enemy stands, when the enemy aims at it or is reloading or turned away. Each mutant leaps with its own strength. (int, pers, wild)
A pounce with a wind-up that steers in mid-air toward a moving enemy. The crouch warns you, then the steering follows you. (int, pers, wild)
An instant pounce that steers in mid-air toward a moving enemy. The steering stays inside the game's own range. The most lethal leap. (int, pers, wild)
A pounce with a wind-up at where a moving enemy will be when it lands. The crouch warns you, then it leaps at your path. (int, pers, wild)
An instant pounce at where a moving enemy will be when it lands. A smarter mutant leads its target more. (int, pers, wild)
The bloodsucker's own leap: it closes the distance to an enemy on a perch, or to a player aiming at it, and strikes with its claws once it lands. It never hits in the air. (int, pers, wild)
A spin-strike when the enemy works around to its back. Whether an individual carries it is settled the moment it appears. (int, pers)

A point-blank pounce with no wind-up, the close strike the chimera otherwise lacks: a vanilla chimera closes to melee range with no attack to use there. It watches for contact constantly and strikes at most every 10 seconds. (int, pers)
A burer throws its gravity attack when you cannot answer it - reloading, unarmed, or with your back turned - the moment its shield is not needed anyway. (int, pers)
Varies the gravity attack's numbers per individual: cooldown, distance band, speed, radius. (wild)
Varies the telekinesis per individual: find radius, distance band, fly speed. (wild)
Varies the psi tube pacing per individual. (wild)
Varies the per-hit stamina drain per individual. (wild)
Varies the aura strength and reach per individual. (wild)
Varies the actor-detection pacing per individual. (wild)
The bloodsucker vanishes to break your aim or a hit while it is still closing, then re-appears when the window ends. Rate-limited, and it never vanishes once at strike range. (int, pers)

Breaks off and runs when near death and far enough to reach safety. A cornered mutant has no room to run and fights to the end. Runs on the inverse of Intelligence: the dull mutant panics. (inv_int, pers, wild)

Healing lets wounded stalkers use the medkits and bandages they carry, and you can see it, as a hurt man limps and a healing one plays the gesture. Vanilla's config leaves out the item lists the healing script reads, and stalkers die with full pockets.
Adds the heal rate, the healing charge by rank, and a pause in healing while he fights. The item lists stay restored with it off.
Scales how much health each heal restores. 2.0 heals twice as fast, and 0.5 half as fast.
The chance a novice carries a healing charge, used when he is hurt with no medkit left. Vanilla gives every rank 50 percent.
The same chance for an experienced stalker.
The same chance for a veteran.
The same chance for a master.
A hurt stalker near you limps while out of combat, standing or walking, matched to the weapon he carries. A fight ends the limp.
The health below which a stalker limps. Lower values wait until he is more badly hurt.
A stalker near you plays a medkit or bandage gesture when he starts to heal, out of combat only.
Accuracy gives each rank a different spread, tight for a legend and wide for a novice. Vanilla has a per-rank curve that Anomaly's rank values leave flat, which gives every stalker the same spread.
Each rank fires with a different spread, wide for a novice and tight for a legend. (Rank)
Higher ranks keep their aim while they fire on the move. (Rank)
Spread for a novice, as a multiple of vanilla. Lower is tighter, and 1.00 is vanilla.
Each rank above novice changes the spread by this much. Negative values tighten it as rank rises.
Spread for a novice while he walks or runs, as a multiple of vanilla. 1.00 is vanilla, and lower is steadier.
Each rank above novice changes his spread on the move by this much. Negative values steady his fire as rank rises.
Higher ranks follow a moving target faster and hold a strafing target longer. (Rank)
How fast a novice's barrel follows a moving target once it is close, in radians per second. 0.24 is vanilla.
Each rank above novice adds this much speed.
How tightly a novice holds a strafing target, as the width of the lock band in radians. 0.196 is vanilla, where a strafing target moves out of his aim.
Each rank above novice widens the band by this much, and higher ranks hold a strafing target longer.
A stalker aims ahead of a moving target by the round's real flight time, and higher ranks lead more truly. (Rank)
How far ahead a novice aims, as a multiple of the correct lead. 2.00 aims twice too far ahead, and 1.00 is exact.
Each rank above novice changes the lead by this much. Negative values bring it toward 1.00 as rank rises.
Higher ranks confirm a threat they glimpse sooner, and a novice stays at the speed of your install. (Rank)
Higher ranks fire shorter bursts more often, and low ranks stay at vanilla. (Rank)
Burst length for a novice, as a multiple of vanilla. Below 1.00 shortens the burst.
Each rank above novice changes the burst length by this much. Keep it at or above the cadence value, or the rate of fire drops.
The pause between a novice's bursts, as a multiple of vanilla. Below 1.00 fires more often.
Each rank above novice changes the pause by this much. Negative values shorten it as rank rises.
How fast a novice turns a glimpse into a confirmed threat, as a multiple of your install. 1.00 is the speed of your install.
Each rank above novice adds this much speed.
How far out a novice starts to notice a threat, as a multiple of your install. 1.00 is the range of your install.
Each rank above novice adds this much range.

A stalker firing with a clear shot keeps his cover, where vanilla moves him whenever it finds a better spot nearby. Losing sight, a blocked shot or an enemy out of range still lets him move. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

When his enemy cannot answer, because he is reloading, empty, unarmed, sprinting, climbing or turned away, a stalker keeps firing past his commitment limit. He moves once the enemy can answer again, and mutants never trigger it. (Intelligence, Personality)
Applies to every stalker outside a maneuver.
The longest stretch a stalker holds an action before vanilla may move him again. He still breaks off as soon as his reason to hold ends.

A maneuver is a complete takeover of a stalker for a real tactical move that vanilla never decides on, like a counterflank, a pickoff or reload cover. The system is built for coordinated, military-style squad tactics, and many more maneuvers are coming. Intelligence decides whether he takes a move, and Personality whether he carries it at all.
Lets AlifeTactics take a stalker over for a maneuver in any fight near you, against you or another stalker. The other Combat pages have separate switches.
No maneuver takes a companion over, and a companion mutant is left alone too.

A stalker hit while standing, or staggered by the hit, holds his place until the reaction ends, where vanilla slides him across the ground. It works on every stalker, in a maneuver or not. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
A stalker fighting someone else turns on you and holds his ground when you come closer than his target. (Intelligence, Personality)

A stalker caught reloading in a watcher's line of fire runs to the nearest cover that hides him, reloading on the way. Unwatched, he reloads where he stands. Inactive on modded exes without this feature. (Intelligence, Personality)

A stalker whose enemy gets inside his weapon's minimum range backs away along a clear lane until he has room to use his weapon, still firing. For example, a sniper backs away from a man with a shotgun. (Intelligence, Personality)

A hurt stalker whose spot is exposed to a nearby enemy falls back to cover behind him, still firing. With no cover in reach he backs off along a clear lane, and two stalkers never take the same cover. (Intelligence, Personality)

A hurt stalker who is the last of his squad puts his weapon away and runs to a friendly base when nobody is shooting at him. A lower Intelligence makes him flee more often. (Intelligence, Personality)

A stalker who outranges his enemy in a standoff holds his position and fires single aimed shots. He stops when the enemy comes close enough to hit back, when he takes fire, or when the enemy has him in sight. (Intelligence, Personality)
Crossfire cuts the damage a stalker deals to stalkers he is not hostile to, and a crossfire between allies stops killing them. Your shots and fights between enemies stay at full damage.
Applies to hits between any stalkers who are not hostile to each other, across factions too.
The share of damage such a hit deals. 0.00 means no damage, and 1.00 is full vanilla damage.

Vision gives each rank a different detection, in how fast a stalker turns a glimpse into a confirmed threat and how far out he starts to notice one. A novice matches your install, and higher ranks notice sooner and farther. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

Danger fixes how stalkers react to a threat they sense, on top of whichever danger scheme your modpack ships. It adds a reaction to distant hits and to a missed knife swing, and it sets how hard NPCs focus on you.

Sound lets hostile stalkers hear you before they see you. Your loud sounds reach the game's hearing, and your quieter steps and handling make them turn or walk over to check. Crouched movement is silent, and your stealth mods keep control of how you are seen.
A stalker hit from far off turns and seeks cover, where vanilla ignores a hit past a distance limit.

A stalker in front of you notices a knife swing that misses him within 3 m. He gets up, raises his weapon and faces you, and a hostile who then sees you fights. A neutral or friend reacts only while Neutral gunfire alert is on.

A neutral or friendly stalker reacts when your bullet strikes near him, a reaction the engine would otherwise drop. He does not turn hostile, and the same switch covers your missed knife swing at a neutral or friend.

Hostile stalkers hear you move. A walk carries 5 m, a sprint 1.6 times farther and a jump landing 10 m, and the surface and rain change the distance. A walk turns him weapon-ready toward the sound, and a sprint or a landing sends him walking over to check.
Hostile stalkers hear your reload within 8 m, an empty click within 6 m and an item use within 5 m. A reload or an empty click sends him walking over, and an item turns him weapon-ready toward you.
A standing stalker out of combat glances toward a creature he hears within 5 to 10 m, a mutant always and a stalker only when he is hostile. He turns his head and stays where he is.
Scales how far your movement and handling noise carries. Below 1.00 makes stealth more forgiving, and above 1.00 lets stalkers hear you from farther.

How strongly an NPC focuses on you while you can see him, against the pull other targets have. 300 weighs you like any other fighter, 900 is the vanilla pull toward you, and 0 removes it. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
Three danger categories once read the wrong config rows through a name collision. Each now reads its own rows.
A mutant corpse no longer crashes the danger time check.
A torn-down NPC reference no longer crashes the danger evaluator.
A bad danger time value no longer crashes the evaluator.
A stalker hit by a bullet knows who shot him. He looks at the shooter's live position and takes cover from it, where vanilla loses the shooter on every hit.
Danger transitions no longer leave a stale lower-body animation playing.
Leaving the danger state clears only its own cover reservation instead of wiping every stalker's.
A corpse despawning mid-investigation no longer crashes the investigator.
Corpse investigation drives the squad member that found the corpse, not the wrong one.
The investigator walks to the cover it found instead of a cleared spot.
The danger check parses its config strings once instead of re-parsing them on every evaluation.
A dead stalker's scripted danger no longer lingers on its id, so a respawn reusing the id starts clean.
The corpse reaction no longer crashes when it fires before its investigation stage is set.

Every vanilla Anomaly and xray bug AlifeTactics fixes, grouped by system, each shown as a locked toggle. The always-on ones cannot be turned off. The rest are switched on their own pages, named in each line.
A stalker is no longer evaluated for danger after he dies, which stops a repeated engine visibility error until the body despawns.

A stalker who held fire because a friend crossed his line no longer stays frozen in a combat stance after the fight ends. The base game drops him without restoring a calm state, so he now returns to normal the moment his enemy is gone.

The base game's hold-fire test blocks a shot for any visible non-enemy standing close in any direction, or standing on the aim line even beyond the target, and its hold re-arms endlessly in a crowd, leaving stalkers aiming in silence for tens of seconds. Those false holds also silenced campers, wounded-finishing, mounted guns and anti-helicopter fire. A stalker now holds and steps aside only for a friend actually between him and his target.

A stalker checks his line of fire for friends against a chimera or burer's body. Vanilla checked it against their feet, because neither creature has the spine bone the check looks for, and logged an engine warning every time.

The base game never cleared a stalker's danger episode memory. Attacked again later, he turned to his first attacker's old position instead of the new threat, and the corpse search animation played only for the first corpse he ever searched. The memory now clears when each danger episode ends.
The distance deciding whether a stalker dodges a grenade or only turns to face it was read on the wrong scale in the base game. The dodge now covers its intended radius around the stalker.
A shot-at stalker turns on the man who hit him, not a distant target he can see. Always on, and needs a recent engine build.
NPCs no longer converge on you about three times harder than on each other. Tuned by the Player target pull slider on Perception, Danger.
A real per-rank accuracy curve replaces vanilla's flat clamp. Needs the Enable Dispersion toggle on Accuracy.
A stalker no longer fires into the low cover he ducks behind. Needs the Cover posture toggle on Conduct.
A hit no longer slides a standing stalker across the ground while the animation plays. Needs the Hit reaction hold toggle on Combat, General and PR #645.
A maneuver never starts on a stalker still playing a hit or script animation. Runs with Maneuvers on builds carrying PR #629.
A stalker's healing charge no longer re-rolls across a save and load.
The bandage gesture waits until the stalker stands still, so his legs no longer freeze and slide. Runs with Healing.
A hurt stalker drops his limp the instant a fight starts. Runs with Healing.
A healing stalker no longer freezes in place or ignores an enemy that appears mid-gesture. Runs with Healing.
A stalker sniped from far off reacts and seeks cover, where a distance gate left him standing. Needs the Distant hits toggle on Danger.
A stalker fires over low cover he can shoot across. The shot check reads eye height, not chest height. Runs with Maneuvers.
Fighters on the vanilla Monolith combat scheme flip between crouch and idle far less often in a fight. Its four actions now count as combat actions for the state manager. Always on.
The medkit and bandage item lists the engine dropped are restored, so NPCs heal reliably. Needs the Healing toggle.
A chimera or lurker waits 3 seconds after any jump before its next one, where vanilla let it jump again the moment it landed. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
Jamming lets NPC weapons jam only from wear. In X-Ray every NPC also rolls an extra jam, and even a new rifle jams, with no jam animation to show it. Your weapon stays as it is.
NPC weapons jam only as their condition wears down.

Ammo lets veteran and higher stalkers fire the armor-piercing rounds they carry, and switch back to standard rounds when those run out. A fight may use up a carried box, sooner for quick-firing weapons and lower ranks. It works only while the game gives NPCs unlimited ammo.
Stalkers who carry armor-piercing rounds load them and use them up fight by fight.

Attachments let stalkers fit the scopes, silencers and grenade launchers they carry to their pistol or rifle, once they are out of a fight with their hands free. A scope then shows on the gun at the next quiet moment.
Stalkers fit attachments from their inventory at the next quiet moment. Story and named characters keep their guns as they are.

Gear lets the artefacts and equipment a stalker carries work for him, by the artefact's anomaly class. The strongest artefact on a channel counts and they do not stack, and a stalker with the air warping around him carries a real artefact.
An artefact gives its carrier up to 10 percent on its channel, and only the strongest counts.
Gravity artefacts and armor plates cut the damage their carrier takes.
Electric and quest artefacts raise the damage their carrier's shots deal.
Thermal artefacts tighten their carrier's aim.
Chemical artefacts give their carrier a slow health restore. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
A stalker carrying any artefact warps the air around him, and you can tell he has one.
A stalker with binoculars sees farther by day. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
A stalker with a night-vision device sees farther at night. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

Debug and development tools. DEBUG log level traces every system with timings: maneuver decisions, danger evaluation, healing ticks and consumed items, per-shot accuracy, ammo and reload events. Written to alifetactics.log. Tracing has a cost, leave at WARN for normal play.
Log verbosity. ERROR: failures only. WARN: anomalies. INFO: module init and patch installs. DEBUG: full per-event tracing with durations.

Write each log line to disk at once instead of buffering. Turn on when diagnosing a crash so the final lines survive a hard freeze that never reaches the periodic flush. Slower, so leave off for normal play.

Live overlay of nearby stalkers: rank and name, health, logic scheme, mental state, and the current target with distance. A green row with the maneuver name in green marks a stalker AlifeTactics is driving, for the maneuver's whole life. Refreshes twice per second and hides while the PDA is open. Pick a corner to show it.

Debug recorder for the physical fight around you. Flags a body that slides (real distance covered with no walk or run animation, including the shove right after a hit) and records shot outcomes: per-rank hit rates split by shooter motion, damage dealt, near misses, and burst lengths per weapon kind, written as tables once a minute. Each line names the system driving that NPC (maneuver, Commitment, or vanilla). Everything goes to alifetactics_world.log. Off costs nothing.
Restore all AlifeTactics MCM settings to defaults. Use after upgrading from a version with a different MCM structure.
Warning: save or discard pending MCM changes first, otherwise they override the reset on the next Accept.
AlifeTactics: all settings restored to defaults.
